title: Game Character
story: You're coding a simple RPG. Your hero has hit points (HP) and a maximum HP. When hit by a monster, HP drops. When drinking a potion, HP rises — but never above the max. You need mutating methods with boundary checks.
why: Methods can enforce rules (like HP clamping) so invalid states are impossible.
analogy: HP is like water in a bucket. `max_hp` is the bucket's brim — you can't hold more than the bucket. Taking damage is pouring water out; you can't have less than empty.
try_it: Add an `is_alive` method that returns `hp > 0`. Add a `health_percent` method that returns `(hp * 100) / max_hp`. Create a character at 30/120 HP and print the percentage.
tips: Clamping means bounding a value between a minimum and maximum — common in games
Check boundaries AFTER the mutation, so you catch the overflow/underflow
Separate damage and healing into methods so the clamping logic lives in one place
common_mistakes: Subtracting without checking for negative HP can make a character undead
Healing without clamping can push HP above max_hp, breaking game balance
